findings.title: A receipt save failure misreports an observed Muse send as not sent
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve .observed when saving its receipt fails and expose the storage error separately. Retain .uncertain for other ambiguous post-click failures; only known pre-click failures may become .notSent. Add failure injection after a matching outgoing message is observed and assert that both returned and in-memory results never claim notSent.
findings.why_it_matters: If the first intent saves succeed, Muse is clicked, a matching outgoing message is observed, and the receipt write or permission update then fails, the catch changes observed to notSent. The UI falsely reports that nothing was sent, and a later repeat is permitted. Preserve the known observation and surface the storage error separately. This is a code-established failure path; storage-failure incidence was not measured.
evidence: MsgBlast/Core/MuseWebSession.swift:168 -- attempt.status = attempt.status == .attempting ? .uncertain : .notSent

MsgBlast/Core/WebServices.swift:36-37 -- attempts.contains { $0.text == text && [.attempting, .uncertain].contains($0.status) }

Trigger: the initial intent and attempting saves succeed, the click runs, and one new matching outgoing message appears; then the filesystem write or permission update for the observed-result save fails.

MsgBlast/Core/MuseWebSession.swift:178-185 mutates the in-memory attempt before throwing filesystem operations; a failed observed-result save enters the outer catch, changes that result to notSent, and the final store can persist the false result if the failure is transient.
findings.validation_reason: MuseWebSession.swift:154-168 mutates an observed attempt before the throwing store, then reclassifies any resulting non-notSent error as notSent, while store at lines 177-185 updates in-memory state before filesystem work and WebServices.swift:36-37 allows retry of notSent; the required post-observation storage failure is reachable from the throwing create/write/permission operations, though its incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Completing a broadcast erases the next draft
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the exact untrimmed shared draft before starting the send and derive the submitted text from it. Clear the draft on completion only if its current value still equals that snapshot (or its revision is unchanged). Add a delayed-send regression that edits the next draft before completion and verifies those edits survive. Keeping the composer editable avoids adding a new input restriction.
findings.first_evidence: MsgBlast/Windows/WebServicesView.swift:223 -- if attempt != nil || id != nil { model.state.draft = ""; model.persist() }
findings.why_it_matters: The shared NSTextView continues writing to AppState.draft while the two submissions are awaited. Completion then clears and persists its current value, erasing a next message typed during that interval. Muse alone can await five seconds of observation. Clear only the submitted draft snapshot, preserving subsequent edits; no app interaction was performed to measure incidence.

findings.title: Publish the Messages comparison before submissions finish
findings.suggested_fix: Split comparison creation from submission: return or publish the ID immediately after `try save()` at line 259, assign `session.state.comparisonID` in the view, then await `model.submit(id, retry: false)` concurrently with `session.send(text)`. Keep the current `sending` guard active until both submissions complete.
findings.why_it_matters: After Send & compare, the native recipient panes remain absent until all Messages sends and their history-observation loops finish, even though the comparison was already saved and individual recipient states are being updated. With multiple recipients this can delay visible native progress by several seconds per recipient, so Muse and Messages do not present independent results as promised. Publishing the saved comparison ID before awaiting submission lets the existing observable comparison state render each recipient's progress immediately.
evidence: MsgBlast/App/AppModel.swift:260 -- await submit(comparison.id, retry: false)
MsgBlast/App/AppModel.swift:313-323 -- for _ in 0..<6 { ... try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(500)) }
findings.validation_reason: AppModel.swift:257-261 saves the comparison but returns its ID only after await submit completes, while WebServicesView.swift:58 and 218-220 cannot render native panes until that returned ID is assigned, and submit can suspend for six 500 ms observations per recipient at lines 313-323; the delay requires at least one native recipient and was not measured in use.

findings.title: Partial broadcast outcomes lack coverage
findings.suggested_fix: Add deterministic tests around the production shared-broadcast orchestration using controlled Muse and Messages operations: Muse fails/Messages succeeds, Muse succeeds/Messages fails, and both fail. Assert independent attempt and comparison outcomes, comparison visibility, and the intended shared-draft behavior. Extract only the small seam necessary to invoke the production path; do not duplicate its logic in tests.

findings.why_it_matters: A normal partial failure can leave Muse and Messages with different outcomes, but the suite only proves the all-success path. Covering both one-side-fails cases at the orchestration boundary makes that contract observable without performing real sends.

triage_groups.title: Shared broadcast completion and progress
triage_groups.context: The shared view awaits both destinations before clearing its draft and publishing the native comparison ID.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix draft preservation (#2), expose the saved native comparison before awaiting delivery (#4), then cover partial outcomes against that production path (#5).
triage_groups.why: These changes share the broadcast orchestration boundary and can use the same controlled-operation test seam.

residual_risks: Live Muse login across app relaunch and compatibility with the deployed frontend remain outside this review. The fixture uses plain DOM listeners; the user supplied a screenshot showing a ready live chat and successful broadcast, but reviewers did not independently reproduce that workflow.

WebWorkspaceState.draft and messageRecipients are unused by the UI; WebServiceTests.swift:69-78 persists the former while the shared composer binds AppState.draft at WebServicesView.swift:179. This is a small storage/test clarity issue, not a reproduced user-facing failure. Unused-callsite inspection used repository text search; external or dynamic references were not established.
testing_gaps: Navigation/loading changes between prepare and click and matching chat DOM on another HTTPS origin have no end-to-end WebKit negative test. These cases exercise the new native-to-page boundary (MuseWebSession.swift:127-142); only the URL predicate is tested off-origin.
Zero or multiple visible Send controls are guarded by MusePageScript.swift:45-47 but not exercised; the existing ambiguous-send test instead suppresses the unique button click handler.
The recovery test covers attempting -> uncertain but not preparing -> notSent, the pre-click recovery branch in WebServices.swift:46-48.
The workflow test waits for final content and does not assert native recipient progress while submissions remain pending; targeted coverage belongs with primary finding #4.
